clue.text: Man wishing each woolly could be cleaner

indicators.note: woolly means fuzzy or muddled, so the letters of these three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man hoping every fleecy item might come up clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' looks like a description of laundry but signals the anagram of MAN WISHING EACH.
explanation.definitionFit: A household appliance that washes clothes is a cleaner in the broad sense.

clue.text: Animal that might give act?

parts.note: read as wordplay, 'wild' would be an anagram signal applied to cat, turning it into act

explanation.surface: Asks which animal might put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: rearranging the word cat gives act.
explanation.definitionFit: A small untamed feline is an animal.

clue.text: Bust flogged to get funds

parts.note: beaten with a strap
for means in order to get, as in 'go for help'
funds are cash

explanation.surface: A sculpture sold off to raise money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like a sculpture and 'flogged' like sold (British slang); Bust is the definition, broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Bust means bankrupt or broke, lacking money, as the idiom does.

clue.text: Article requires hi-tech the writer rejected

parts.note: IT, information technology, is the hi-tech field

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, me

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece that needs advanced technology the author turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: An article in the sense of a single thing or entry in a list.

clue.text: It makes hot water muddy grey around London area

indicators.note: around says the mixed letters go round the London area
muddy means to cloud or confuse, so the letters of grey are mixed

parts.note: SE is the south-east London postal district

explanation.surface: Something that turns grey murky around London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddy' looks like a description of the water but is the anagram signal; SE is London's south-east postal area.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot spring that erupts, or a British gas water heater, both produce hot water.

clue.text: Dreadful, getting tooled up to support the French uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue the second part sits below the first, supporting it
in a down clue an uprising reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: la is French for the
tooled up is slang for armed, so getting tooled up is arming

explanation.surface: A terrible French revolt as people take up weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns LA upwards to AL; 'to support' puts ARMING under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something frightening or disturbing is dreadful.

clue.text: Fifteen pantomime figures

definitions.meaning: a rugby union team has fifteen players; this is a London club
the masked, diamond-costumed clowns of traditional pantomime

explanation.surface: A troupe of fifteen pantomime characters.
explanation.walkthrough: Harlequins is a London rugby union club; a rugby side is a fifteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous rugby team (a fifteen) and the clowns of commedia and pantomime.

clue.text: Local with spotted head causes viewer's complaint

parts.note: local means nearby, near
spotted means seen, sighted
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A neighbour with a pimply head spoils someone's view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted head' suggests acne; 'spotted' means seen and 'head' a promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to focus on distant objects is an eye condition, a complaint of sight.

clue.text: Given food that keeps set, being whipped

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the word for set goes within

parts.note: given food means fed
to lay is to set down, place

explanation.surface: Fed with set food while being punished.
explanation.definitionFit: Flayed means beaten or lashed so the skin comes off, as by whipping.

clue.text: In the main gallery exhibits change

indicators.note: the word gallery shows a change, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Mostly, an art gallery rotates what it puts on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gallery' and 'exhibits' suggest an art show; 'exhibits change' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonymous phrases: something true in the main is true mostly, for the greater part.

clue.text: It's a far-reaching message, on paper

definitions.text: It's a far-reaching message, on paper

parts.words: It's a far-reaching message, on paper
parts.note: a letter sent overseas by plane travels far, and is written on thin paper

explanation.surface: A written note whose influence spreads widely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far-reaching' suggests influential, but here means literally travelling a long way, by air.
explanation.definitionFit: Post carried by aircraft reaches distant countries, a cryptic description of overseas letters.

clue.text: The Law of Clipped Woodland

indicators.note: clipped means trimmed, so the word for woodland loses its last letter

parts.note: a copse is a small wood

explanation.surface: Reads like the title of a strange rural statute.
explanation.definitionFit: Police officers are informally called the law, as in 'run from the law'.

clue.text: Smoothly made as a one-piece?

definitions.meaning: a garment made in one piece has no joins sewn in it

explanation.surface: Describes something manufactured perfectly, in a single piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, without seams, as a one-piece garment is; figuratively, without visible breaks or hitches.

clue.text: Last instruction from ENT nurse?

definitions.meaning: an ear, nose and throat nurse might ask you to put your tongue out

explanation.surface: A nurse's final words to a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective (final) but is the verb, to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to persevere through difficulty, and literally to protrude something such as a tongue.

clue.text: Contract requiring three partly to supply occasional items

indicators.note: only some letters, every other one, are taken from the two words

explanation.surface: A contract that needs three parties to provide intermittent goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to supply occasional items' takes alternate letters: TRE from 'three' and ATY from 'partly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal agreement between states is a kind of contract.

clue.text: Satisfied to see delta after eluding storms

indicators.note: after says the delta letter follows the rearranged letters
storms suggests violent upheaval, so the letters of eluding are thrown about

parts.note: Delta is the radio alphabet word for the letter D

explanation.surface: Pleased to reach a river delta having escaped bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storms' looks like weather in the scene but is the anagram signal, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfied as a verb: to indulge a craving or a person is to gratify it.

clue.text: A red van's going around galleries

indicators.note: going around suggests turning about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A red van driving round art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: Open roofed porches along a house front, sometimes called galleries.

clue.text: Overcome being pretentious

definitions.meaning: showy, putting on airs, as an adjective

explanation.surface: Someone who has defeated their pretentiousness.
explanation.definitionFit: One word with two senses: emotionally moved, and artificial or showy in manner.

clue.text: Rat afloat, first one pursuing craft

indicators.note: afloat suggests drifting loose, so the letters of rat are moved about

parts.note: first is written 1ST, read as IST

explanation.surface: A rat floating along, leading the way behind a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests a boat to go with 'afloat'; here it means skill. 'afloat' rearranges RAT to ART.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter or sculptor practises a creative skill, a craft.

clue.text: Couples coming from Dorset in urge to head west

indicators.note: to head west says the hidden letters are read backwards
coming from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pairs of people arriving from Dorset, driven by a wish to travel west.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Couples coming' is not a synonym; 'Couples' alone is, and 'coming from' signals the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples as a verb means joins together, a synonym.

clue.text: They're made to run where it's freezing his legs off

definitions.text: They're made to run where it's freezing

indicators.note: off suggests gone wrong or disordered, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone forced to run in the cold until his legs fall off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' suggests a person; the runners are on snow vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sledges pulled across snow glide on runners in icy places.

clue.text: Troop's physical restraint right out the window

definitions.note: troop is, a singular noun with the verb attached

indicators.note: out the window means discarded, so the letter is thrown out

parts.note: a leg iron shackles the ankle

explanation.surface: A soldier's shackles are no longer in use.
explanation.definitionFit: A large body of soldiers, a unit or troop.

clue.text: Following spell inside, had a bite with daughter over

parts.note: a spell is a period of time, a term
inside means in
to have a bite is to eat, here in the past tense

explanation.surface: After a spell indoors, someone ate with their daughter round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like part of the story (daughter came over) but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is over has finished or been brought to an end.

clue.text: Creep giving lip

definitions.meaning: to move slowly and cautiously, as a verb
the rim or brink of something

explanation.surface: A sneaky person giving cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: One word: to inch along gradually, and the border or rim of something.

clue.text: Web links the compiler with mum

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me
mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: An internet page connects the setter with their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother; here it means keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A web is a net or network of strands, as a mesh is.

clue.text: Eats having been swimming?

parts.note: eats is slang for food; fish and shellfish were swimming before they were caught

explanation.surface: Someone eating after a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eats' looks like a verb but is the noun, slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish and shellfish eaten as food once lived in the ocean, swimming.

clue.text: Something at the greengrocer's that's mostly under water

definitions.meaning: a variety of crisp lettuce sold by fruit and vegetable sellers
a floating mass of ice, most of which is submerged

explanation.surface: A grocer's item that is largely submerged.
explanation.walkthrough: A greengrocer is a British shop selling fruit and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a crisp lettuce variety and a floating ice mass with most of its bulk below the sea.

clue.text: Images backing US city article — second is making things greener

parts.note: photos are images

indicators.note: backing says the city's abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: NY is New York
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Pictures supporting an American city's essay on going green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making things greener' sounds environmental but is literal: plants turning green.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants use light to make chlorophyll-driven food, the process that keeps foliage green.
